newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Westpac defends small business competition.
newsitem.headline: Westpac defends small business competition.

text.p: Westpac Banking Corp managing director Bob Joss, responding to a government call for more competition in the small business sector, said on Monday the big banks were already providing strong competition for the sector.
"We think the big banks do a very good job of looking after the small business sector and we're getting more competitive," Joss said told a Securities Insitute of Australia luncheon.
Treasurer Peter Costello has ruled out mergers between Australia's Big Four banks until they improve competition the small business sector.
Joss said that in comparison with overseas markets, margins for small business lending in Australia were actually lower than those in other countries such as the United States.
"I can tell you because I've worked in both markets that our small business customers attract smaller lending spreads than small business does in America," he said.
"From a spread point of view, we're actually in quite a competitive position in Australia," he said.
He said small business lending attracted higher margins than large business lending and home mortgage lending because their default rates over the longer term were much higher.
Joss said that on average, six to 10 percent of small business loans defaulted over a five year period while less than one in 1,000 home loans defaulted.
